chronoseries.name: Aurelia
chronoseries.what_changes_at_this_node: This is the only node, at 0 Ma. Nothing in the series is older or younger. The change that the mathematics can show at this age is between the living diffusion ratio D_v/D_u = 20, which admits a 201 µm mode, and the equal-diffusion control D_u = D_v = 1, which does not. A sub-wavelength cellular patch (domain shorter than λ_c) also refuses the mode. A millimetre-scale rhopalium would fit several repeats of the same wavelength; it would not change λ_c.

scale.label: 201 µm
scale.meaning: Turing pigment stripe / ocellus wavelength inside one rhopalial pigment cup. Not the bell diameter. Not the arc length between neighbouring rhopalia.

equations.pde_u: du/dt = Du * laplacian(u) + gamma * (a - u + u^2 * v)
equations.pde_v: dv/dt = Dv * laplacian(v) + gamma * (b - u^2 * v)
equations.jacobian: fu = gamma*(-1 + 2*u*v*), fv = gamma*u*^2, gu = gamma*(-2*u*v*), gv = gamma*(-u*^2)

boundary_conditions: Periodic on a square patch whose side is 3 critical wavelengths (about 601.8 µm). The patch is one ocellus neighbourhood, not the whole bell.

parameters.note: These numbers are for this 201 µm Holocene node. They are not taken from the sibling stub abrams-aurelia-aurita-turing-wavelength.

empirical_claims: Aurelia develops rhopalia, and each rhopalium bears a pigment-cup ocellus (Nakanishi, Hartenstein & Jacobs 2009).
A scyphozoan medusa has eight rhopalia (Helm 2018). Eight is an anatomical count. It is not L_bell / 201 µm.
A two-species reaction-diffusion system can select a finite wavelength when the inhibitor diffuses sufficiently faster than the activator (Turing 1952; Schnakenberg 1979).
No source consulted here measures that Aurelia ocellus pigment wavelength as 201 µm. The length is the assigned detail scale.

specimen.what_it_shows: Several living Aurelia aurita medusae in aquarium light. Oral views show four gonad arcs. The photograph does not resolve 201 µm.

reported_in_source: Turing 1952 linear instability of a reaction-diffusion system and the existence of a finite critical wavelength.
Nakanishi, Hartenstein & Jacobs 2009: Aurelia rhopalia develop a pigment-cup ocellus.
Helm 2018: scyphozoan medusae have eight rhopalia.
Thoma 2015 CC0 photograph of living Aurelia aurita.
reconstructed_in_script: Jacobian numbers a=0.10, b=0.90, Du=1, Dv=20, gamma=1, chosen so the critical wavelength equals 0.0002006 m.
Spectral Lie–Trotter integration, dispersion curve sampled from the PDE, equal-diffusion ablation, and Dv sweep.
Bell circularity and coherency measured on the Karlsruhe photograph.
transfer_boundary: The 201 µm figure is a scale assignment, transferred onto Schnakenberg wavelength selection. It is not a fit to a histological measurement.
does_not_claim: That a published study measured an Aurelia pigment wavelength of 201 µm.
That eight rhopalia are produced by counting 201 µm waves around the bell margin.
That the Karlsruhe photograph is a micrograph of the ocellus.
That the gallery tile datasets/species_gallery/.../Aurelia_aurita.jpg is a primary specimen. It was not used.
